title: LogEntry
description: What happened — append-only journal entry. Source file: governance/log.json ({"entries": [LogEntry]}). AI_LOG.MD is the generated view. No silent finishes: a task cannot reach accepted without a log entry referencing it.

title.description: One sentence in the past tense naming what changed and the record ids it settles. Real example: "The prune stopped eating the two files deploy promises never to overwrite (I-0152, I-0153)" (L-0285). "fixed hook" is eight words of jargon that name neither the hook nor what stopped being wrong.

what_was_done.description: The EVIDENCE, not a story: the verify command and its rc, the diffstat, and every refusal hit and what was done about it. Real example: "harness deploy's seeding lane creates project-standards.md and project-walls.conf create-if-absent; the I-0143 prune then removed any path the previous manifest names that payload.list lacks. Fixed by writing each seeded path into seeded.list and skipping it in the prune. sh tests/harness-tests.sh rc=0; 3 files changed, 61 insertions" (L-0285). "created X, verified Y" carries nothing a reader who was not present can check.

verification.description: Evidence the acceptance check passed — command output, file, screenshot ref; the EVIDENCE block verbatim. Real example: "Planted first: 11 new assertions in tests/harness-tests.sh shown FAILING against 444dfd1 in a detached worktree, including 'deploy DESTROYED .claude/rules/project-standards.md because a previous manifest claimed it'. After the fix: harness-tests exits 0" (L-0285). A check planted before it passed is worth more than one that was green from the start.

pending.description: What is knowingly not done, and why it is safe to leave. Real example: "seals.json is a record records-check reads and is correctly left out, so the first views render on a never-sealed target still leaves that one file untracked".
